6bqBsHSwPgw.summary: DIY Perks builds a realistic artificial sun for dark winters, using a powerful water-cooled LED, a satellite dish reflector for near-parallel rays, and a scattering layer to mimic the blue sky. The video explains the optics behind why most lamps do not look like sunlight and shows the build and its results.
6bqBsHSwPgw.why: Whenever HN discusses seasonal affective disorder, myopia, or bright home lighting, people point to this as the most convincing buildable example of sunlight-like illumination.

60z_hpEAtD8.summary: An animated introduction to geometric algebra, presented as a language that can describe most of physics. It was made with manim and covers multivectors and how they generalize familiar tools like cross products and quaternions.
60z_hpEAtD8.why: HN calls it the best video on geometric algebra, one that makes the subject click in about 40 minutes.

6y8XgGhXkTQ.summary: The first part of Innuendo Studios' six-part video essay series on the online hostility around Anita Sarkeesian and GamerGate. It lays out the history and the motivations of the people involved.
6y8XgGhXkTQ.why: HN recommends the series as a nuanced analysis of online harassment, defensiveness, and gaming culture conflict.

6avJHaC3C2U.summary: Dylan Beattie's NDC London talk on code written for art, fun and curiosity rather than utility. It includes quines, live music programming with Sonic Pi, and a memorable closing.
6avJHaC3C2U.why: HN regularly names it among the best programming talks ever, praising the storytelling, the demos and the ending.

6UsHHOCH4q8.summary: A Last Week Tonight segment on how tobacco companies sustain profits by pushing sales overseas. It covers suits against countries like Australia over plain packaging through trade-deal arbitration.
6UsHHOCH4q8.why: HN uses it in TPP and trade-deal threads as a clear example of ISDS being used by corporations against governments.

6mTbuzafcII.summary: Rich Hickey introduces transducers in Clojure, a way to make map, filter and similar algorithms composable independent of the data source. This avoids duplicated implementations and intermediate collections across sequences, channels and streams.
6mTbuzafcII.why: HN treats it as the original and definitive explanation of transducers, recommended whenever the concept comes up.

6orsmFndx_o.summary: A TV show about Ivan Sutherland's 1963 MIT thesis software Sketchpad, which ran on the TX-2 computer. It shows a light pen drawing, constraints, snapping, scaling and object-style graphics, foundations of GUIs and CAD.
6orsmFndx_o.why: HN returns to it as a striking demonstration that core GUI, CAD and constraint-programming ideas existed in the 1960s.

6h3RJhoqgK8.summary: Mike Monteiro's Creative Mornings talk "Fuck You, Pay Me" with his lawyer Keith Levine, on contracts, scope creep and making sure designers and freelancers get paid. This copy has Portuguese subtitles.
6h3RJhoqgK8.why: Recommended to freelancers and consultants as practical advice on contracts and getting paid.

6RhtiPefVzM.summary: Engineering Explained works through whether electric cars are really worse for the environment than gasoline cars. It covers battery production emissions, the electricity mix used to charge, and how long an EV takes to break even on lifetime emissions.
6RhtiPefVzM.why: HN commenters link it repeatedly as a clear, number-based rebuttal to the claim that EVs are worse for the climate than gas cars.

62tIvfP9A2w.summary: Vox Earworm explains why John Coltrane's Giant Steps is so hard to improvise over: it is fast and moves through three keys. Musicians Braxton Cook and Adam Neely walk the host through the underlying music theory.
62tIvfP9A2w.why: Recommended as a well-produced, accessible explanation of Giant Steps and the harmonic ideas behind Coltrane's work.

66YRCjkxIcg.summary: Practical Engineering explains pumped storage hydropower, which makes up most grid-scale electricity storage. It covers how it works and why it fits only certain geographies.
66YRCjkxIcg.why: Recommended as a clear explanation of pumped hydro and its limits in energy storage discussions.

6EghiY_s2ts.summary: Actress Claudia Christian tells how she overcame alcoholism using the Sinclair Method, which uses naltrexone to gradually reduce cravings. She discusses fresh perspectives on treating alcohol use disorder.
6EghiY_s2ts.why: HN commenters share it as the talk that introduced them to the Sinclair Method as an alternative approach to alcohol dependence.

6wBrOV2FJM8.summary: A maker's time-lapse of building a working computer inside a LEGO-style brick, using a tiny 0.42-inch OLED screen, with a demo at the end.
6wBrOV2FJM8.why: HN finds the miniaturization mind-blowing and cites it as a standout example of surreal hobbyist technology.

6AeWu1fZ7bY.summary: Benno Rice's BSDCan 2018 talk on why systemd exists and what it got right and wrong. It traces the history of Unix init and why Linux distributions adopted it, while asking what the BSDs should learn.
6AeWu1fZ7bY.why: HN recommends it as a balanced, eloquent take on the systemd debate that even skeptics find persuasive.

6BhV-o77RqQ.summary: A DIY demonstration of a fan-and-screen mosquito trap that uses carbonated water as a CO2 attractant. The creator reports catching about 8,000 mosquitoes in two nights.
6BhV-o77RqQ.why: HN commenters point people to it as a cheap, simple, effective way to kill mosquitoes, and some report trying it successfully.

6OPsH8PK7xM.summary: Polylog explains how algorithms can be turned into circuits and encoded as satisfiability problems, which lets you effectively run them backwards. It uses this to motivate breaking RSA, general reductions to SAT, and what P vs NP is really asking.
6OPsH8PK7xM.why: Recommended as an intuitive, animated explanation of P vs NP framed around reversing computation.

6VOQnK7O2To.summary: Jason Calacanis interviews investor Chris Sacca on This Week in Startups. Sacca discusses what makes a founder, his investments such as Kickstarter, and his personal story of losing money and recovering.
6VOQnK7O2To.why: HN recommends it in startup video lists for its stories and Sacca's candid background.

6ZYLp5uX9Yw.summary: Jim Pavloff rebuilds The Prodigy's 'Voodoo People' in Ableton from its listed samples. The video shows how the track is assembled and how close a handmade reconstruction can sound.
6ZYLp5uX9Yw.why: Used as an example of prototyping music and, in a Copilot copyright thread, of a handmade reconstruction that sounds like the original.

6c_LeIXrzAk.summary: Musician Adam Neely examines whether certain keys sound sadder than others, looking at the history of tuning systems and temperaments and at how instrument timbre shapes the emotional character we hear. It draws on historical aesthetics writing and audio examples.
6c_LeIXrzAk.why: HN commenters recommend it for its historical context on tuning systems and for how instruments influence what music gets composed.

6p8zAbFKpW0.summary: A Last Week Tonight segment explaining carbon offsets, what they claim to do, and how they may worsen climate change. It looks at perverse incentives and questionable projects.
6p8zAbFKpW0.why: HN points to it as an informative explainer on why many carbon offset schemes are not genuine.

6gmP4nk0EOE.summary: Michael Wesch's five-minute video about Web 2.0, showing how the read/write web, XML and user-generated content change how people create and share information.
6gmP4nk0EOE.why: Cited as a classic, compact explanation of the read/write web and open data, invoked in threads on the semantic web and open APIs.

6ihrGNGesfI.summary: Deviant Ollam gives a long talk on risk and preparedness: get a lawyer, passport, locksmith and other resources before you need them. It covers practical steps to build defenses against serious problems in life.
6ihrGNGesfI.why: Recommended as a thorough preparedness talk, and cited for specifics such as lawyers, password managers and gun ownership.

6reLWfFNer0.summary: Pieter Levels talks at Dojo Bali about building startups without venture capital through bootstrapping, persistence and learning many skills as a generalist. He reviews his own past projects.
6reLWfFNer0.why: Pointed to as an inspiring talk for solo makers turning side projects into profitable businesses.

60OVlfAUPJg.summary: Conrad Wolfram argues that the part of math taught in schools, hand calculation, is tedious and mostly irrelevant to real mathematics. He proposes teaching math through computer programming so students can tackle real problems.
60OVlfAUPJg.why: Cited in HN discussions of math and CS education reform as an argument that school math is boring because it is taught wrong.

62jZENi1ed8.summary: Steve Hsu's 2011 Google Tech Talk reviews psychometric measurement of intelligence and the heritability of adult IQ, then discusses genome-wide association studies seeking the genes behind cognitive ability.
62jZENi1ed8.why: Pointed to as a well-cited hour on IQ and genetics whenever intelligence and heritability come up.

63vqob-MljQ.summary: The official music video for Kylie Minogue's Come Into My World, directed by Michel Gondry, built around a looping scene with multiplying copies of Kylie.
63vqob-MljQ.why: Cited as a landmark looping music video, a reference point for creative video and editing tricks.

64cEmjtwRgw.summary: Cody's Lab builds a prototype algae growing panel as an experiment before making more. The channel also shows growing algae for consumption.
64cEmjtwRgw.why: Pointed to as a cheap, hands-on example of home algae cultivation.

6Af6b_wyiwI.summary: Bill Gates's 2015 TED talk, given after the 2014 Ebola outbreak, argues the world is unprepared for the next fast-spreading epidemic. He calls for scenario planning, vaccine research, and trained health workers, in the way countries prepare for war.
6Af6b_wyiwI.why: During COVID-19 HN commenters cited it as a prescient pandemic warning.

6Cf7IL_eZ38.summary: Corning's 2011 concept video showing a future where specialty glass surfaces and touchscreens are woven into everyday life.
6Cf7IL_eZ38.why: Referenced as an inspiring example of a vision-of-the-future video with believable everyday uses.

6JAgXz6xO0s.summary: The trailer for Tim Hunkin's series The Secret Life of Components, eight guides to mechanical and electromechanical parts for designers and makers.
6JAgXz6xO0s.why: Recommended to people who like building things, as part of Hunkin's body of practical engineering explainers.

6JwEYamjXpA.summary: Matt Parker's Royal Institution talk based on his book Humble Pi, covering everyday mathematical mistakes and spurious patterns that went wrong in engineering and software. It mixes stand-up comedy with stories of coincidence and error.
6JwEYamjXpA.why: Used as a funny, accessible reference for coincidences, spurious patterns and maths errors.

6K8NkJpUei4.summary: A roughly 40-minute Mahalo mentor interview with Elon Musk, covering his background from Zip2 and PayPal to SpaceX, Tesla and SolarCity, along with advice for entrepreneurs.
6K8NkJpUei4.why: Shared as an early long-form Musk interview, notably for his answer about what motivates him.

6Maq5IyHSuc.summary: Big Clive gives a 38-minute beginner's guide to identifying common electronic components and what they do. He keeps the maths minimal and aims to fill gaps for people just starting out.
6Maq5IyHSuc.why: Suggested as a gentle starting point for beginners in electronics.

6Nfqpr3ygSg.summary: A short comparison of the retail release of Metallica's Death Magnetic against the Guitar Hero 3 version of the same song. It switches between the two so you can hear and see the heavy clipping in the retail master.
6Nfqpr3ygSg.why: HN uses it as the go-to demonstration of the loudness war and what over-compressed mastering does to music.

6NlI4No3s0M.summary: A short demonstration comparing just intonation with equal temperament, played so you can hear how the tuning compromise changes intervals and chords. It includes a Bach prelude played in both tunings.
6NlI4No3s0M.why: Shared as a quick audible demonstration of the errors that equal temperament introduces compared with pure intervals.

6b4ZZQkcNEo.summary: A short Boston Dynamics clip of the Sand Flea, an 11-pound RC-car-style robot that can jump about 30 feet into the air. An onboard stabilization system keeps it oriented in flight and for landings.
6b4ZZQkcNEo.why: Brought up as a favorite and as an inspiration for small, cheap jumping robots for obstacle crossing and planetary exploration.

6chLw2aodYQ.summary: A 2007 Google Tech Talk in which Bryan Cantrill demonstrates DTrace and explains how it improves debugging of both development and live production systems.
6chLw2aodYQ.why: Recommended as the DTrace creator's own demonstration and a reference for dynamic tracing.

6qD9XElTpCE.summary: Peter Shor tells the story of how he discovered Shor's Algorithm, from his early mathematics days to the quantum factoring breakthrough. It was recorded at MIT at the Physics of Computation conference.
6qD9XElTpCE.why: HN recommends it as an oral history of the algorithm straight from its inventor.

6wZmYMWKLkY.summary: A short product demo of Dabble DB, a web tool for importing, entering and manipulating structured data with little effort. It was built in Smalltalk and later acquired by Twitter.
6wZmYMWKLkY.why: Used as a reference for an ahead-of-its-time end-user database tool, brought up in threads on Access clones, Smalltalk and data-entry tools.

67tHtpac5ws.summary: A two-minute clip in which Milton Friedman uses a humble pencil to show how thousands of strangers across many countries cooperate, without central direction, to make a simple product. It is a short visual version of the 'I, Pencil' essay's argument about free markets and dispersed knowledge.
67tHtpac5ws.why: HN commenters cite it as the quick, shareable illustration of hidden supply-chain complexity and decentralized knowledge, and bring it up in threads on AI, manufacturing and specialization.

6BBx8BwLhqg.summary: A three-minute demonstration with a decommissioned 4 tesla MRI magnet showing how magnetic objects are pulled in and oscillate along the bore. It illustrates the safety hazards of ferromagnetic items near MRI scanners.
6BBx8BwLhqg.why: Linked in threads on magnets and implants as a vivid demonstration of how violent MRI magnet forces are.

6Chp12sEnWk.summary: A Black Hat USA 2017 briefing by the prosecutors who caught Russian carder Roman Seleznev. It covers the electronic evidence collected, the international trail, and how he was located and arrested.
6Chp12sEnWk.why: Pointed to as a true-crime story of cybercrime investigation, usually in passing.

6G59zsjM2UI.summary: A long Joe Rogan Experience podcast episode with psychologist Jordan Peterson and biologist Bret Weinstein, recorded during the controversy at Evergreen State College. They discuss campus politics, polarization, ideology and related social topics.
6G59zsjM2UI.why: HN commenters cite it as a wide-ranging conversation on political polarization and free discussion, and one commenter points to a segment on wealth distribution following a square-root law.

6SYHamnHqU8.summary: Laura Try recounts her 3,000-mile row across the Atlantic as part of a crew of four women in the 2018 Talisker Whisky Atlantic Challenge.
6SYHamnHqU8.why: Cited as an example of ocean rowing crossings and recommended by one commenter as really good.

6_yU9eJ0NxA.summary: Numberphile talks with Grant Sanderson of 3Blue1Brown about a darts puzzle with a shrinking bullseye. Solving it takes the volumes of high-dimensional spheres, and the answer turns up Euler's number.
6_yU9eJ0NxA.why: Used as a friendly example of high-dimensional geometry showing up in a simple problem, and of ball volume shrinking inside a hypercube.

6aIA2LaB2Iw.summary: Andrew Price presents at the Blender conference on the problems, politics and possible fixes for Blender's user interface, followed by a full Q&A. He argues that an interface upgrade is overdue.
6aIA2LaB2Iw.why: Cited as an example of how hard it is to reconcile UX views in open source communities, and as the start of a redesign discussion.

6bG5ps5KdDo.summary: Cambridge Analytica CEO Alexander Nix keynotes the OMR 2017 marketing festival on big data and personality-based targeting in political campaigns. It was given before the company's scandal broke.
6bG5ps5KdDo.why: HN cites it, often critically, as Nix openly describing data-driven manipulation and targeting methods.

6egeUxIEQnM.summary: Matt Parker of Stand-up Maths explains why people keep making the same mistake with millions and billions, using a Bloomberg cash calculator example. He looks at the unit slip behind the repeated arithmetic error.
6egeUxIEQnM.why: HN links it to explain why people repeatedly get large-number arithmetic wrong in discussions of money and mental math.

6i72czkSUsM.summary: A one-minute clip posted by Canadian politician Pierre Poilievre featuring Bill Maher criticizing Justin Trudeau's remarks about unvaccinated people.
6i72czkSUsM.why: Cited in HN threads on the 2022 Canadian trucker convoy and emergency powers as an example of criticism of Trudeau from a liberal commentator.

6m3GuoaxRNM.summary: Ori Bernstein gives an overview of Plan 9 at a NYC*BUG meeting. He explains what the system is, how it is built, what has happened since Bell Labs, and what its design teaches, with a live demo.
6m3GuoaxRNM.why: HN mostly cites it as background on Plan 9 and its ideas, with one commenter thanking the speaker for an enjoyable talk.

6n2eDcRjSsk.summary: Daniel Stenberg's keynote at FrOSCon 2025 on AI slop attacks on the curl project, with examples of bogus AI-generated security reports. He discusses the toll on maintainers and why various countermeasures don't fit the project.
6n2eDcRjSsk.why: HN points to it when discussing AI-generated bug reports and vibe-coded pull requests burdening open source maintainers.

6xWXRk3yaSw.summary: MKBHD reviews the Fisker Ocean electric SUV and concludes it is the worst car he has reviewed, going through its many problems. He warns viewers not to buy this version of the car.
6xWXRk3yaSw.why: Mostly cited in discussions of Fisker's troubles and of whether a negative review can sink a car company.

6yqfmXiZTlM.summary: An AWS re:Invent 2019 session for advanced DynamoDB users on design patterns used by large customers, including Amazon retail. It covers GSI sharding, index overloading, graph processing, composite keys and transactional workflows.
6yqfmXiZTlM.why: Recommended as Rick Houlihan's definitive talk on modeling relational-style data in DynamoDB.

6yqi0FabHHs.summary: Joe Scott takes a serious look at space sunshades as a climate fix, asking how big they would need to be, what they would cost and whether they would work. He draws on Roger Angel's paper and launch options.
6yqi0FabHHs.why: Linked as a worked look at the maths and assumptions of orbital sunshades, which concludes they are impractical.

62kxPyNZF3Q.summary: The shareholder speech by Larry the Liquidator, played by Danny DeVito, from the film Other People's Money. He argues that a dying company should be liquidated rather than kept alive.
62kxPyNZF3Q.why: Quoted in threads about declining companies and shrinking markets as a blunt statement of the case for liquidation.

6AXPnH0C9UA.summary: A mashup of a Sesame Street Count clip with a Lemon Demon song, where the swear words are censored in absurd ways. It is a short comedy piece about censorship.
6AXPnH0C9UA.why: Brought up in censorship threads as a joke and as a canonical example of censorship that changes the meaning of the original.

6COvD8oynmI.summary: Simon Peyton Jones's first lecture on types in Haskell from the Oregon Programming Languages Summer School 2013. It covers type classes and how they relate to OOP, subtyping and polymorphism.
6COvD8oynmI.why: Mostly cited by timestamp for specific explanations, such as how type classes map to OOP and why QuickCheck is a great type class example.

6CXRaTnKDXA.summary: A clip from The Newsroom season 3 in which characters argue that the climate change debate is over and only a technology to reverse emissions can help.
6CXRaTnKDXA.why: Dropped into climate threads as a fictional but relevant fatalistic take, not as a recommendation.

6DezodR9hNI.summary: Tiffany Fong's phone interview with Sam Bankman-Fried shortly after FTX filed for bankruptcy. He discusses the alleged backdoor, FTT collateral, political donations, and his legal position.
6DezodR9hNI.why: HN cites it for what SBF said himself, especially his claims about political donations and the backdoor allegation.

6IwqmezeSuQ.summary: A short clip, published by The Sun, of a Russian surface-to-air missile that appears to turn around after launch and hit its own launch site. It was reportedly filmed in Alchevsk during the 2022 war in Ukraine.
6IwqmezeSuQ.why: Used as a joke whenever a stray or malfunctioning Russian munition is in the news.

6Jx_bJgIFhI.summary: Tom Scott visits Dinorwig Power Station in Wales, a pumped-storage hydro plant often called Britain's largest battery. He explains how it works and how its role has shifted from TV pickup spikes to balancing wind and solar.
6Jx_bJgIFhI.why: HN cites it whenever grid storage or pumped hydro comes up, as an accessible example of storage at scale.

6OYyXv2l4-I.summary: A short 2019 clip of Chuck Schumer's January 2017 warning to Trump that the intelligence community has many ways of getting back at him.
6OYyXv2l4-I.why: HN uses it mostly in critical arguments about intelligence agencies and government power over speech and privacy.

6QCF8tVqM3I.summary: A one-minute clip by cpddan reproducing how a Tesla on Autopilot 2.5 may have steered into a gore point barrier, as in a fatal Highway 101 crash.
6QCF8tVqM3I.why: HN cites it as evidence of Autopilot's behavior around lane gores, mostly in critical comments about Tesla.

6VixqvOcK8E.summary: A BBC Politics Live interview in which Andrew Neil presses conservative commentator Ben Shapiro on his past statements and an incident involving Corey Lewandowski and a reporter. It is a tense, widely shared exchange.
6VixqvOcK8E.why: Mentioned as an example of Shapiro struggling under tough questioning, and sometimes in critical political comments.

6WGKz2sUa0w.summary: Steve Mould shows that LEDs and solar panels are both diodes made from semiconductors, so a solar panel can emit light and an LED can generate electricity. He demonstrates a small solar panel lighting up.
6WGKz2sUa0w.why: Cited as a neat demonstration that diodes work in both directions in semiconductor and LED discussions.

6WTdTwcmxyo.summary: The official music video for Tommy Tutone's 1981 hit 867-5309/Jenny. The chorus is built around a phone number.
6WTdTwcmxyo.why: HN links it to explain the cultural reference when 867-5309 shows up as a stand-in phone number.

6akmv1bsz1M.summary: Veritasium explores what general relativity says about black holes, white holes and wormholes, with help from physicists Geraint Lewis and Juan Maldacena. It introduces Penrose diagrams and the idea that other universes may be implied.
6akmv1bsz1M.why: Cited in black hole threads as an approachable introduction to Penrose diagrams and what happens inside a black hole.

6bODiZ5bP84.summary: LGR reviews the Book 8088 and Hand 386, newly built DOS retro PCs sold on AliExpress that use real legacy chips on custom boards. He covers what is neat about them and their compromises and odd design decisions.
6bODiZ5bP84.why: Linked when retro hardware, 8088 or 386 machines, or oddball AliExpress computers come up.

6eZ2yvWl9nQ.summary: Footage of Bungie's Jason Jones revealing Halo to the public at Macworld on July 21, 1999. It shows the early third-person version of the game.
6eZ2yvWl9nQ.why: Cited as a historical reference that Halo was first announced at Macworld, with Steve Jobs involved, and nearly launched as a Mac game.

6epzmRZk6UU.summary: The official 1986 music video for Paranoimia by Art of Noise featuring the computer-generated TV personality Max Headroom. It is a synth-pop and sampling-era piece of 80s pop culture.
6epzmRZk6UU.why: HN mentions it mostly as a reference point in Max Headroom threads, as the essential Art of Noise tie-in to that 80s character.

6iCPIUGnHQ8.summary: A short upload of the classic ICQ notification sounds, such as the 'uh-oh' message alert.
6iCPIUGnHQ8.why: Linked for nostalgia, as an instant audio time-travel to the early instant messaging era.

6kg4vVYKc90.summary: A YouTuber explores the Chernobyl zone in 2013, takes a gamma spectrum of a hot reactor fuel fragment, and jokes about a radioactive ant bite. It is a hands-on amateur look at radiation in the exclusion zone.
6kg4vVYKc90.why: Cited as an example of Chernobyl YouTuber content and of casual handling of radioactive material.

6lZMr-ZfoE4.summary: A compilation of the first four iPhone commercials from the June 2007 launch. The ads walk through using the device and stress real web browsing.
6lZMr-ZfoE4.why: Cited as a reference for how Apple's early iPhone advertising was product-focused and used usage walkthroughs.

6rbJu10Telc.summary: Omar Rizwan's short !!Con talk about writing a Breakout game in JavaScript that runs inside a PDF. It explores the surprisingly large PDF specification, including its scripting support.
6rbJu10Telc.why: Cited as the fun, surprising example of how much a PDF can do, and the talk behind the Horrifying PDF Experiments repo.

6uSVVCmOH5w.summary: Eric Parker connects a fresh Windows XP machine to the internet in 2024 to see how quickly it gets infected with malware. He documents the dangers of running an unpatched legacy OS online.
6uSVVCmOH5w.why: HN uses it as the counterpoint to a story where XP survived online, noting that a directly exposed XP machine is infected within minutes, though some critics say the setup is not representative of typical use.

6uvQTTPr9Rw.summary: A very short demo of SmackBook, a hack that used the MacBook Pro's sudden motion sensor so that smacking the sides of the laptop switches desktop spaces.
6uvQTTPr9Rw.why: HN cites it as a fun example of novel uses of the MacBook motion sensor whenever laptop accelerometers come up.

6yN2H3--1aw.summary: A one-minute satirical clip of a person trying to pass as a normal guy with the line "Did you see that ludicrous display last night?". It parodies awkward small talk about sports.
6yN2H3--1aw.why: HN uses it as a joke about nerds faking normalcy or sports small talk.
